resumen: Sitting on a bench with the back rest at about 30°, you press two dumbbells from the upper chest until the arms are straight. Like the incline barbell press, but each arm on its own.
ejecucion: Set the back rest to about 30° and sit with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
Lie back on the back rest, bringing the dumbbells to the sides of your upper chest, feet on the floor.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight, bringing them slightly together over your upper chest.
Lower under control until the dumbbells are at chest level, elbows slightly below your shoulders.
When you finish, bring the dumbbells to your thighs before sitting up, instead of dropping them to the sides.
matices: The studies on bench inclination used a barbell: in one with thirty trained people, the upper chest was most active at 30°, and above 45° the anterior deltoid took over. We have found no study measuring inclination with dumbbells; the effect is assumed to be similar, and dumbbells let each arm follow its own path.
